food_name: Ground turmeric (NIST SRM 3299; research reference material)
food_database: NIST Standard Reference Material 3299 Certificate of Analysis
raw_or_processed_state: Ground rhizome powder; irradiated reference material; research use only
food_use_classification: food-associated matrix; reference material is not for human consumption
synonym_verification_status: Exact analyte named as Curcumin by NIST; Stage B identity crosswalk retained from registered target
mapping_review_rationale: NIST SRM is a turmeric rhizome reference material for research and method validation and is explicitly not for human consumption. Its certified concentration is strong quantitative composition evidence for this specific material, but it must not be used as an ordinary edible turmeric exposure record without project policy review.
moisture_basis: Dry-mass basis; NIST moisture correction 0.9146 g dry mass/g as-received mass
analytical_method: NIST LC-absorbance (LC-UV) at 425 nm plus collaborating laboratories LC-absorbance and LC-fluorescence; gravimetric calibrants; combined certified-value assignment
extraction_method: 100 mg test portions; methanol extraction by end-over-end rotation 15 min plus ultrasonication 15 min; centrifugation; mixed-mode C18-phenyl separation
sample_size: NIST duplicate 100 mg portions from each of 10 packets, plus collaborating-laboratory interlaboratory results; certified uncertainty at approximately 95% confidence
source_title: Standard Reference Material 3299: Ground Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) Rhizome, Certificate of Analysis
database_reference: Certificate Table 1; pages 1–3; also Rimmer et al. 2020, J AOAC Int 103(6):1625–1633, DOI 10.1093/jaoacint/qsaa048
source_classification: National metrology institute certified reference material; supporting interlaboratory analytical study
source_verification_status: NIST certificate inspected; certified value is 12.17 ± 0.56 mg/g dry mass; mass-fraction traceability and methods described
extraction_notes: NIST certificate says SRM 3299 is ground turmeric rhizome powder, intended for analytical validation and similar matrices. The certified value combines NIST and collaborating-lab results; uncertainty is expanded U95%. Exact Stage B registered curcumin target ID carried over.
uncertainty_notes: This is not an ordinary food-market sample: NIST explicitly labels the SRM research use, not human consumption. It is irradiated after packaging, and variety/geography are not reported. Keep held and exclude from edible exposure mappings unless project rules explicitly permit using reference materials as food-composition evidence.
